text:
dmitri: Quick thought — propose we try a policy-driven write-steering prototype that uses short-lived consent tokens + a soft-escrow handshake for PII-heavy tenants. Goal: deterministic active/active routing without full geo-locks.
kevin: hmm, can you sketch the handshake? how is escrow different from our current escrow proposals? :thinking:
maya: tl;dr: escrow here is lightweight — just a token that proves 'consent + region preference' signed by control plane. Dataplane uses token to accept writes locally or forward. no heavy state transfer.
ash: @dmitri curious: how do we avoid split-brain if tokens expire mid-swap?
dmitri: good q. idea is a decay window + prefer-local-with-grace. token has expiry + "decay_ttl" metadata. during swap, proxies will accept local writes if token present OR if last-seen token within decay window. after window, we fall back to canonical consent lookup (slower) and may reroute.
kevin: sounds like an availability vs correctness knob. We should make decay window configurable per-tenant. some enterprises will want strict residency (zero decay).
maya: agreed. add per-tenant policy: mode = {strict, preferred, permissive}. strict => no decay, forward to resident region only. preferred => short decay (30s). permissive => longer (5m).
ash: what about auditing? need clear logs for any write that crossed residency because legal teams will ask.
ash: propose we emit an event: "write_routing_decision" with fields: tenant, request_id, origin_region, routed_region, reason=(token|decay|policy_fallback).
ops-bot: deploy-check: infra note — proxies must be able to validate token signature locally (public key cache) and fall back to control-plane validation on miss. caching window required.
ash: cryptographic note — tokens should be ECDSA-signed and include fingerprint of tenant KMS key to revoke quickly if needed.
kevin: perf question — will this add latency on cold path? signature verify is cheap but control-plane fallback is heavy. we should ensure local cache hit rate >99.9% for keys.
maya: we can pre-warm keys on tenant attach and rotate via push. also provide a transparent verification library for proxies.
dmitri: implementation sketch: 1) control plane issues consent token when tenant config changes. 2) client includes token in x-residency-consent header. 3) edge proxy validates; if valid and policy allows, serve locally. 4) if invalid/expired -> check cache -> if within decay_window allow with reason=decay. else call control-plane sync endpoint (sync may return allow/deny) and emit audit event.
ash: edge cases: what about cross-tenant shared models that have different residency needs? If model inference runs in different region, we must surface that to the tenant and maybe deny.
kevin: add a model-residency tag. tokens should carry allowed_model_regions. otherwise deny.
maya: rollout plan: A) lab sim with synthetic PII tenants B) canary region with permissive mode C) add strict mode gating via admin toggle.
dmitri: experiments to measure: percent of routed-writes that used decay vs token vs control-fallback; avg extra latency on fallback; audit event volume.
ash: one more thing — failure mode if control-plane is partitioned: proxies must default to conservative behavior (prefer resident region) for strict tenants, and permissive for dev/test tenants. we need a per-tenant default.
kevin: noted. Also we should document operator runbook: how to revoke a token quickly, how to abort a swap mid-flight, how to query audit traces.
maya: i'll draft an RFC summary + sequence diagrams tomorrow. tagging @ashley for legal review on audit semantics and retention. :+1:
ash: thanks all. if no objections I'll start a small spike next week to validate cache hit assumptions.
ops-bot: reminder: create a feature-flag before canary.
ash: ack.
